chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever travels or marries while the moon is in Scorpio will not see the goodness.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the moon being in Scorpio for travel and marriage in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi reflects the Shia tradition of 'ilm al-ruqya' (astrological omens), linking celestial movements to earthly outcomes, specifically advising against travel or marriage when the moon is in Scorpio (Al-Aqrab). It underscores the belief that cosmic alignments can influence the reception of 'al-husna' (goodness/blessing), a concept deeply rooted in both popular piety and scholarly discussions on natural signs.

en.hubeali: H 14864 – A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Bin Humraan, from his father, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘
The one who travels or gets married whilst the moon is in the Scorpio will never see the goodness’.
en.sarwar: 417. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Bin Humraan, from his father, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said: ‘
